results.description: Constantly hums an off-key tune, even during tense moments.
Refers to themselves in the third person when nervous.
Collects small stones and insists each one is "special."
Apologizes to inanimate objects after bumping into them.
Never sits with their back to a door.
Punctuates sentences with a nervous, wheezing laugh.
Has only a single tooth.
Often giggles in very inappropriate situations.
Always uses a signature phrase at the end of conversations.
Spits a lot when speaking.
Likes to speak in riddles.
Cracks every knuckle before making a decision.
Refuses to walk under ladders or scaffolding.
Speaks to plants as though they can answer back.
Names every weapon they carry.
Sniffs food twice before taking a bite.
Answers every question with another question.
Hums the same three notes when thinking.
Keeps a tally of every coin ever owed to them.
Bites their lip when lying.
Insists on tasting a drink before serving it to anyone.
Never removes their gloves in public.
Talks about themselves exclusively in the past tense.
Collects the buttons off other people's coats.
Whistles a funeral dirge when nervous.
Refuses to sit at the head of any table.
Counts their steps under their breath while walking.
Sleeps sitting upright, never lying down.
Introduces themselves with a different name every time.
Cannot resist correcting other people's grammar.
Keeps every receipt, no matter how small the purchase.
Salutes strangers out of old habit.
Speaks louder the more nervous they become.
Draws small symbols in the dirt while waiting.
Refuses to be the first to leave a room.
Constantly rearranges other people's belongings.
Winks after every joke, even the unfunny ones.
Only trusts people who share their birth month.
Talks to their own shadow when alone.
Cannot pass a mirror without checking their reflection.
Insists every story they tell is completely true.
Chews on the end of a quill even when not writing.
Keeps a locked box that they claim is empty.
Bows slightly to animals as a greeting.
Repeats the last word someone says to them.
Believes every left shoe brings bad luck.
Cleans their weapon obsessively after every use.
Never finishes a meal, always leaving one bite.
Speaks to the dead as if they were listening.
Insists on paying in the exact coin, never more.
Taps twice on any door before entering, even their own.
Keeps their back to open windows whenever possible.
Refuses to say the number thirteen aloud.
Wears a single earring, though never explains why.
Laughs before delivering bad news.
Never lets anyone else pour their drink.
Recites a short prayer before crossing any bridge.
Insists on shaking hands with their left hand.
Cannot tell a lie without laughing first.
Keeps every letter ever sent to them, even threats.
Speaks only in short, clipped sentences when afraid.
Refuses to travel after sundown.
Always sits facing the nearest exit.
Draws a small mark on any door they pass through.
Never raises their voice, even in an argument.
Insists on naming any horse they ride, even a borrowed one.
Repeats their own name quietly before falling asleep.
Keeps a stone in their pocket they call a good luck charm.
Cannot stand the sound of scraping metal.
Always finishes another person's sentence for them.
Wears their weapon on the wrong hip on purpose.
Insists that every scar has a story, even the small ones.
Changes the subject rather than admit being wrong.
Keeps count of every lie they've ever told.
Speaks to strangers as though they were old friends.
Always removes their hat indoors, even in pouring rain.
Cannot resist reading any letter left unattended.
Insists on sharpening even a butter knife.
Refuses to eat food that has touched the edge of the plate.
Talks in their sleep, always in a different voice.
Keeps a tally of every insult ever received.
Always walks around puddles, never through them.
Insists every stranger looks familiar somehow.
Cannot resist humming along to any tune, even a funeral hymn.
Wears a ring on a cord instead of a finger.
Never lets their drink be refilled past the halfway mark.
Speaks with an accent that seems to change by the day.
Always double-knots their boots, even indoors.
Refuses to be measured for new clothing.
Keeps a list of everyone who has ever wronged them.
Insists on being the one to light the fire.
Cannot pass a beggar without leaving something small.
Always sniffs a letter before reading it.
Speaks fondly of a sibling that no one has ever met.
Refuses to whistle indoors.
Keeps their money in a different pocket every day.
Insists on carrying an umbrella, rain or shine.
Cannot resist petting any animal, however dangerous.
Always leaves a small offering at crossroads.
Speaks of the future as though it has already happened.
Refuses to be the last one awake at camp.
Keeps a single glove, though the pair was lost years ago.
Insists that every debt be repaid in person.
Cannot resist finishing a crossword or puzzle left behind.
Always greets strangers with a compliment, sincere or not.
Speaks of an old rival by a nickname no one else uses.
